title: Finite evaluation of the normalized system reduction/pullback square
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E/Q_l, Operations o, a RealizationModel model, schemes X,Y, a morphism f:X→Y, an arbitrary H in the completed integral derived category on Y, and n≥0. Define integralFiniteScalarPull(f,n) by transporting the existing PurCompactSupport.scalarPull for reduction modulo exponent n+1 along finiteReductionIso at X,Y and the derived finitePullbackIso. Evaluation at n of model.reductionPull(f)_H, followed by pullbackTensorDerivedEvaluation(f,n) at reduction(H), followed by finite pullback of reductionEvaluation(Y,n)_H, equals reductionEvaluation(X,n) at ringedPull(f)(H) followed by integralFiniteScalarPull(f,n)_H. This is a pullback statement before taking any open mates and requires no open immersion, constructibility or completeness.

source.place: Coefficient comparisons of evaluation and adjunction units/counits; open evaluation component of the original node plan, Step 2; Lean split from lean/Sheaf/SixFunctors/IntegralSupportProjectionTransport.lean, original proof docstring lines 28–45

proof.text: At the ordinary module level, transpose the proposed square through the two composite adjunctions. The reduction evaluation and sequence inverse evaluation are normalized by their scalar and geometric units. The OrdinaryLimitModel.projections equation and the sectionwise identity of finiteScalarRestrictionDirect identify the right projection square. Naturality of units and injectivity of the composite transpose give the ordinary square, degreewise on complexes.

On a flat-term K-flat complex P, geometric inverse image remains good. Evaluate RealizationModel.model and use completedQuotientReductionPresentation at X,Y, the defining cochain normalization of pullbackTensorDerivedEvaluation, and the ordinary square from the first step. Cancel the finite scalar and geometric computation isomorphisms and apply integralFiniteScalarPullCochainModel. This proves the theorem at Q(P).

Both sides are components of natural transformations. The localization of the full subcategory of flat-term K-flat complexes is the entire integral derived category. Localization.natTrans_ext therefore extends the equality on Q(P) to every H.

proof_origin.place: The scalar/pullback comparison on a flat-term K-flat representative in the finite-evaluation argument; Stacks Tags 07A6, 06YY and 0D6E.

lean.statement:
theorem integralReductionPullFiniteSquare (o : Operations l E)
    (model : RealizationModel l E o) {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (H : Integral l E Y) (n : ℕ) :
    (coefficientSequenceDerivedEvaluation l E X n).map ((model.reductionPull f).hom.app H) ≫
      (pullbackTensorDerivedEvaluation l E f n).hom.app ((calculus l E Y).reduction.obj H) ≫
      (finiteDerivedPullback l E n f).map (((calculus l E Y).reductionEvaluation n).hom.app H) =
    ((calculus l E X).reductionEvaluation n).hom.app ((ringedPull l E f).obj H) ≫
      (integralFiniteScalarPull l E f n).hom.app H
